subject.title: docs(durable): rebuild beta3 durable core RFC and proof plan

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a new general durable-core layer beyond the durable task, subagent, delivery, lease, audit, flow, and restart-recovery mechanisms already present on the target base?
rationale: The RFC gates a broad dependent implementation with new persistent and configuration surfaces, while current repository direction disfavors duplicative heavy orchestration without explicit technical and product sponsorship.

options.title: Narrow to missing invariants
options.body: Revise the RFC around concrete cross-owner gaps and stable architecture, then reassess the dependent implementation.

options.title: Sponsor the full durable core
options.body: Explicitly approve the broader substrate and own its schema, configuration, migration, privacy, and operator support burden.

options.title: Stop the durable stack
options.body: Close the RFC and dependent stack if current owner-specific durability remains the intended architecture.

recommendation.title: Narrow to missing invariants
recommendation.body: Revise the RFC around concrete cross-owner gaps and stable architecture, then reassess the dependent implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across the existing durable storage surfaces and repository product direction.
